statement: If from a medial area there be subtracted a medial area incommensurable with the whole, the two remaining irrational straight lines arise, either a second apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.
heath_proof: For, as in the foregoing figures, let there be subtracted from the medial area BC the medial area BD incommensurable with the whole; I say that the “side” of EC is one of two irrational straight lines, either a second apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole. For, since each of the rectangles BC, BD is medial, and BC is incommensurable with BD, it follows that each of the straight lines FH, FK will be rational and incommensurable in length with FG. [X. 22] And, since BC is incommensurable with BD, that is, GH with GK, HF is also incommensurable with FK; [VI. 1, X. 11] therefore FH, FK are rational straight lines commensurable in square only; therefore KH is an apotome. [X. 73] If then the square on FH is greater than the square on FK by the square on a straight line commensurable with FH, while neither of the straight lines FH, FK is commensurable in length with the rational straight line FG set out, KH is a third apotome. [X. Deff. III. 3] But KL is rational, and the rectangle contained by a rational straight line and a third apotome is irrational, and the “side” of it is irrational, and is called a second apotome of a medial straight line; [X. 93] so that the “side” of LH, that is, of EC, is a second apotome of a medial straight line. But, if the square on FH is greater than the square on FK by the square on a straight line incommensurable with FH, while neither of the straight lines HF, FK is commensurable in length with FG, KH is a sixth apotome. [X. Deff. III. 6] But the “side” of the rectangle contained by a rational straight line and a sixth apotome is a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole. [X. 96] Therefore the “side” of LH, that is, of EC, is a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

**Statement:** If from a medial area there be subtracted a medial area incommensurable with the whole, the two remaining irrational straight lines arise, either a second apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

**Step 1.** Let AB be a medial area, and from it let the medial area CD be subtracted, where CD is incommensurable with AB. We must show that the side of the remaining area (AB minus CD) is either a second apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole.

**Step 2.** Set out a rational straight line EF [D10.1.3]. Apply the medial area AB to EF, producing EG as breadth, so that AB equals the rectangle EF by EG [1.45]. Apply the medial area CD to EF, producing EH as breadth (with H between E and G), so that CD equals the rectangle EF by EH [1.45]. Then the remaining area AB minus CD equals the rectangle HG by EF.

**Step 3.** Since AB is a medial area applied to the rational straight line EF, the breadth EG is rational and incommensurable in length with EF [10.22]. Since CD is a medial area applied to the rational straight line EF, the breadth EH is rational and incommensurable in length with EF [10.22].

**Step 4.** Since AB equals EF times EG and CD equals EF times EH, we have AB is to CD as EG is to EH [6.1]. Since AB and CD are incommensurable, EG and EH are incommensurable in length [10.11].

**Step 5.** Since EG is rational and EH is rational, the squares on them are commensurable with the square on EF, and therefore the squares on EG and EH are commensurable with one another [10.12]. Since EG and EH are incommensurable in length, they are rational straight lines commensurable in square only.

**Step 6.** Therefore HG, which is the remainder when EH is subtracted from EG, is an apotome [10.73]. And EF is rational. So the side of the rectangle HG by EF (which equals the remaining area) is determined by the type of apotome that HG is [10.91, 10.92, 10.93, 10.94, 10.95, 10.96].

**Step 7.** Now, EG is incommensurable in length with EF (Step 3), and EG is the whole of the apotome HG. Also, EH is incommensurable in length with EF (Step 3), and EH is the annex of the apotome HG. Since neither the whole EG nor the annex EH is commensurable in length with the rational straight line EF, HG cannot be a first apotome [D10.3.1], a second apotome [D10.3.2], a fourth apotome [D10.3.4], or a fifth apotome [D10.3.5].

**Step 8.** Therefore HG is either a third apotome or a sixth apotome. These are distinguished by whether the square on EG is greater than the square on EH by the square on a straight line commensurable or incommensurable in length with EG [D10.3.3, D10.3.6]. Both cases can arise depending on the particular medial areas chosen.

**Step 9.** Case 1: If HG is a third apotome, then since the area HG by EF is contained by a rational straight line EF and a third apotome HG, the side of this area is a second apotome of a medial straight line [10.93].

**Step 10.** Case 2: If HG is a sixth apotome, then since the area HG by EF is contained by a rational straight line EF and a sixth apotome HG, the side of this area is a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole [10.96].

**Step 11.** Therefore, if from a medial area there be subtracted a medial area incommensurable with the whole, the side of the remainder is either a second apotome of a medial straight line or a straight line which produces with a medial area a medial whole. Q.E.D.
